title: Why do we have day and night?
question: Does night come because the sun moves, or because the Earth turns?
steps: Drag the Earth left or right with your finger to turn it.
See whether the fox's house is on the side facing the sun or on the other side.
Watch the sky over the fox's yard change in the window below.
observe: The half facing the sun has day, the other half has night. As the Earth turns from west to east, the fox's house goes through morning, noon, evening and night in turn.

terms.name: Axis
terms.description: An invisible rod through the middle of the Earth, joining its north end and its south end.

terms.name: Rotation
terms.description: The Earth turning about its axis from west to east, once a day.

terms.name: Day and night
terms.description: The side facing the sun gets sunlight and has day; the other side gets none and has night.

law.title: The Earth's rotation, day and night
law.description: The Earth turns about its axis once a day, from west to east. The sun stays still: the side facing it has day, the other side night. The Earth's turning brings day and night.

tip: Drag the Earth left or right with one finger: it turns as far as your finger moves. It stops as soon as you let go, and it turns either way. The orange arrow at the north end shows the way the Earth really turns (from west to east).
tip_short: Drag the Earth left or right to turn it

predict.question: Does night come because the sun moves, or because the Earth turns?
predict.reason: The sun stays still. As the Earth turns, the fox's house goes to the side away from the sun, and night comes.
predict.bridge: Turn the Earth yourself and find out!

stages.text: Turn the Earth so the sun is highest over the fox's house!
stages.say: When the fox's house faces the sun straight on, it is noon. Then the sun is at its highest.
stages.miss: Turn it to face the sun!

stages.text: Make it night at the fox's house, to see the fox's favourite star!
stages.say: When the fox's house is on the side away from the sun, no sunlight reaches it. So it is night and the stars come out.
stages.miss: Turn it away from the sun!

stages.text: Make it morning at the fox's house, just as the sun comes up!
stages.say: The Earth turns from west to east. So the sun always rises in the east. Morning is where the fox's house is just turning out of the night into the sun.

story.keeper: This is my home. For days the sun hasn't come up properly, and it stays dark…
story.clue: Something sparkled by the house! A piece, maybe? It's too dark to see.
story.map_clue: Up the hill, where the big globe is!

kid.intro: This is the day and night lab. Imagine an invisible rod through the middle of the Earth, joining its north end and its south end. It is called the **axis**.

intro_more.text: The Earth spins about this axis like a top, once a day. This is called **rotation**. It always turns from west to east.
The side facing the sun has day, the other side has night.

kid.title: Turn the Earth to change day and night!
kid.say: The side facing the sun has day, the other side night. The Earth's turning brings day and night.
kid.tip: Drag the Earth left or right to turn it.

note.law: The side facing the sun has day, the other side night. The Earth turns once a day, and that brings day and night.
